sanskrit: etat te pārtha rājyaṃ ca striyo ratnāni caiva ha iṣṭān prāṇān ahaṃ hīmāṃs tyakṣyāmi ripusūdana
english: This kingdom is yours, O Pārtha, and the women, and the jewels too; for I, O slayer of foes, shall now give up this dear life of mine.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ sa bībhatsur mātulena paraṃtapaḥ durmanā dīnamanasaṃ vasudevam uvāca ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by his maternal uncle, Bībhatsu, the scorcher of foes, with a heavy heart spoke these words to the despairing Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ vṛṣṇipravīreṇa madhubhiś caiva mātula vihīnāṃ pṛthivīṃ draṣṭuṃ śaktaś ciram iha prabho
english: O my uncle, O lord, I cannot long endure to look upon an earth bereft of that foremost hero of the Vṛṣṇis and of the Madhus.

sanskrit: rājā ca bhīmasenaś ca sahadevaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ nakulo yājñasenī ca ṣaḍ ekamanaso vayam
english: The king, and Bhīmasena, and Sahadeva the Pāṇḍava, and Nakula, and the daughter of Yajñasena — we six are of one mind.

sanskrit: rājñaḥ saṃkramaṇe cāpi kālo 'yaṃ vartate dhruvam tam imaṃ viddhi saṃprāptaṃ kālaṃ kālavidāṃ vara
english: The hour has surely come for the king's own departure as well. Know that this time has arrived, O best of those who know the seasons of time.

sanskrit: sarvathā vṛṣṇidārāṃs tu bālavṛddhāṃs tathaiva ca nayiṣye parigṛhyāham indraprastham ariṃdama
english: By all means, O tamer of foes, I shall take the wives of the Vṛṣṇis, the young and the old alike, into my charge and lead them to Indraprastha.

sanskrit: ity uktvā dārukam idaṃ vākyam āha dhanaṃjayaḥ amātyān vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ draṣṭum icchāmi māciram
english: Having said this, Dhanaṃjaya spoke these words to Dāruka: I wish to see the counsellors of the Vṛṣṇi heroes without delay.

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā vacanaṃ sudharmāṃ yādavīṃ sabhām praviveśārjunaḥ śūraḥ śocamāno mahārathān
english: Having spoken these words, the heroic Arjuna, mourning for those great car-warriors, entered the Yādava assembly hall, Sudharmā.

sanskrit: tam āsanagataṃ tatra sarvāḥ prakṛtayas tathā brāhmaṇā naigamāś caiva parivāryopatasthire
english: When he had taken his seat there, all the subjects, and the Brāhmaṇas, and the townsmen gathered round and stood before him.

sanskrit: tān dīnamanasaḥ sarvān nibhṛtān gatacetasaḥ uvācedaṃ vacaḥ pārthaḥ svayaṃ dīnataras tadā
english: To all of them, dejected in mind, subdued, and bereft of their senses, Pārtha — himself more dejected still — then spoke these words.

sanskrit: śakraprastham ahaṃ neṣye vṛṣṇyandhakajanaṃ svayam idaṃ tu nagaraṃ sarvaṃ samudraḥ plāvayiṣyati
english: I shall myself lead the people of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas to Śakraprastha; but this whole city the ocean shall overwhelm.

sanskrit: sajjīkuruta yānāni ratnāni vividhāni ca vajro 'yaṃ bhavatāṃ rājā śakraprasthe bhaviṣyati
english: Make ready your conveyances and your jewels of every kind. This Vajra shall be your king at Śakraprastha.

sanskrit: saptame divase caiva ravau vimala udgate bahir vatsyāmahe sarve sajjībhavata māciram
english: On the seventh day, when the spotless sun has risen, we shall all dwell beyond these walls. Make ready without delay.

sanskrit: ity uktās tena te paurāḥ pārthenākliṣṭakarmaṇā sajjam āśu tataś cakruḥ svasiddhyarthaṃ samutsukāḥ
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha of untiring deeds, the townsfolk swiftly made themselves ready, eager for their own welfare.

sanskrit: tāṃ rātrim avasat pārthaḥ keśavasya niveśane mahatā śokamohena sahasābhipariplutaḥ
english: That night Pārtha passed in the dwelling of Keśava, suddenly overwhelmed by a vast bewilderment of grief.

sanskrit: śvobhūte 'tha tataḥ śaurir vasudevaḥ pratāpavān yuktvātmānaṃ mahātejā jagāma gatim uttamām
english: When the morrow came, the glorious Vāsudeva, scion of Śūra, of great splendour, composed himself in yoga and passed to the highest goal.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdo mahān āsīd vasudevasya veśmani dāruṇaḥ krośatīnāṃ ca rudatīnāṃ ca yoṣitām
english: Then there arose a great and terrible clamour in Vāsudeva's house, of women crying aloud and weeping.

sanskrit: prakīrṇamūrdhajāḥ sarvā vimuktābharaṇasrajaḥ urāṃsi pāṇibhir ghnantyo vyalapan karuṇaṃ striyaḥ
english: With dishevelled hair, their ornaments and garlands cast aside, beating their breasts with their hands, the women wailed piteously.

sanskrit: taṃ devakī ca bhadrā ca rohiṇī madirā tathā anvāroḍhuṃ vyavasitā bhartāraṃ yoṣitāṃ varāḥ
english: Devakī and Bhadrā and Rohiṇī and Madirā, those foremost of women, resolved to follow their lord upon the pyre.

sanskrit: tataḥ śauriṃ nṛyuktena bahumālyena bhārata yānena mahatā pārtho bahir niṣkrāmayat tadā
english: Then, O Bhārata, upon a great bier borne by men and decked with many garlands, Pārtha carried the scion of Śūra forth from the city.

sanskrit: tam anvayus tatra tatra duḥkhaśokasamāhatāḥ dvārakāvāsinaḥ paurāḥ sarva eva nararṣabha
english: And after him there followed, smitten with pain and grief, all the townsmen who dwelt in Dvārakā, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tasyāśvamedhikaṃ chatraṃ dīpyamānāś ca pāvakāḥ purastāt tasya yānasya yājakāś ca tato yayuḥ
english: His parasol from the horse sacrifice, and the blazing sacred fires, and the priests went on before that bier.

sanskrit: anujagmuś ca taṃ vīraṃ devyas tā vai svalaṃkṛtāḥ strīsahasraiḥ parivṛtā vadhūbhiś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: And those queens, beautifully adorned, followed that hero, surrounded by thousands of women and by daughters-in-law by the thousand.

sanskrit: yas tu deśaḥ priyas tasya jīvato 'bhūn mahātmanaḥ tatrainam upasaṃkalpya pitṛmedhaṃ pracakrire
english: In that place which had been dear to the great-souled one while he lived, they laid him out and performed the funeral rites for the dead.

sanskrit: taṃ citāgnigataṃ vīraṃ śūraputraṃ varāṅganāḥ tato 'nvāruruhuḥ patnyaś catasraḥ patilokagāḥ
english: Then the four wives, fair-limbed and seeking the world of their lord, ascended the pyre after that hero, the son of Śūra, when he had been placed upon the fire.

sanskrit: taṃ vai catasṛbhiḥ strībhir anvitaṃ pāṇḍunandanaḥ adāhayac candanaiś ca gandhair uccāvacair api
english: And the son of Pāṇḍu had him, attended by those four women, burned with sandalwood and with fragrances of every kind.

sanskrit: tataḥ prādurabhūc chabdaḥ samiddhasya vibhāvasoḥ sāmagānāṃ ca nirghoṣo narāṇāṃ rudatām api
english: Then there arose the sound of the kindled fire, and the chanting of the Sāman singers, and the weeping of men as well.

sanskrit: tato vajrapradhānās te vṛṣṇivīrakumārakāḥ sarva evodakaṃ cakruḥ striyaś caiva mahātmanaḥ
english: Then the young sons of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, with Vajra at their head, and the women too, all offered the water-libations to the great-souled one.

sanskrit: aluptadharmas taṃ dharmaṃ kārayitvā sa phalgunaḥ jagāma vṛṣṇayo yatra vinaṣṭā bharatarṣabha
english: Having had this rite duly performed without omitting any sacred duty, Phalguna went, O bull of the Bharatas, to the place where the Vṛṣṇis had perished.

sanskrit: sa tān dṛṣṭvā nipatitān kadane bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ babhūvātīva kauravyaḥ prāptakālaṃ cakāra ca
english: Beholding them fallen in that slaughter, the descendant of Kuru was sorely grieved, and he performed for them the rites due at such a time.

sanskrit: yathāpradhānataś caiva cakre sarvāḥ kriyās tadā ye hatā brahmaśāpena musalair erakodbhavaiḥ
english: He then performed all the rites in due order of rank for those who had been slain by the Brāhmaṇa's curse with the clubs sprung from the eraka grass.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarīre rāmasya vāsudevasya cobhayoḥ anviṣya dāhayām āsa puruṣair āptakāribhiḥ
english: Then, having sought out the bodies of both Rāma and Vāsudeva, he had them cremated by trusted men.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ vidhivat kṛtvā pretakāryāṇi pāṇḍavaḥ saptame divase prāyād ratham āruhya satvaraḥ aśvayuktai rathaiś cāpi gokharoṣṭrayutair api
english: Having duly performed the funeral rites for them, the Pāṇḍava set out in haste on the seventh day, mounting his car, with chariots yoked to horses and others drawn by oxen, mules, and camels.

sanskrit: striyas tā vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ rudatyaḥ śokakarśitāḥ anujagmur mahātmānaṃ pāṇḍuputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: The women of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, weeping and wasted with grief, followed after the great-souled son of Pāṇḍu, Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: bhṛtyās tv andhakavṛṣṇīnāṃ sādino rathinaś ca ye vīrahīnaṃ vṛddhabālaṃ paurajānapadās tathā yayus te parivāryātha kalatraṃ pārthaśāsanāt
english: The servants of the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, the horsemen and the car-warriors, and the townsmen and country-folk, bereft of their heroes, old and young, went surrounding the women at Pārtha's command.

sanskrit: kuñjaraiś ca gajārohā yayuḥ śailanibhais tathā sapādarakṣaiḥ saṃyuktāḥ sottarāyudhikā yayuḥ
english: The elephant-riders went mounted on elephants like unto mountains, attended by their foot-guards and equipped with their upper weapons.

sanskrit: putrāś cāndhakavṛṣṇīnāṃ sarve pārtham anuvratāḥ brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś caiva mahādhanāḥ
english: And the sons of the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, all devoted to Pārtha, the Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras of great wealth, went with him.

sanskrit: daśa ṣaṭ ca sahasrāṇi vāsudevāvarodhanam puraskṛtya yayur vajraṃ pautraṃ kṛṣṇasya dhīmataḥ
english: Sixteen thousand women of Vāsudeva's inner apartments went forth, placing at their head Vajra, the grandson of the wise Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: bahūni ca sahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca bhojavṛṣṇyandhakastrīṇāṃ hatanāthāni niryayuḥ
english: And many thousands, millions, and tens of millions of women of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas, their lords slain, went forth.

sanskrit: tat sāgarasamaprakhyaṃ vṛṣṇicakraṃ maharddhimat uvāha rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pārthaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: That host of the Vṛṣṇis, vast as the ocean and of great prosperity, Pārtha — best of car-warriors, conqueror of hostile cities — led onward.

sanskrit: niryāte tu jane tasmin sāgaro makarālayaḥ dvārakāṃ ratnasaṃpūrṇāṃ jalenāplāvayat tadā
english: When that people had gone forth, the ocean, the abode of sea-monsters, overwhelmed with its waters Dvārakā, that city filled with jewels.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam abhiprekṣya dvārakāvāsino janāḥ tūrṇāt tūrṇataraṃ jagmur aho daivam iti bruvan
english: Beholding that wonder, the people who dwelt in Dvārakā hastened on ever more swiftly, crying, 'Ah, this is fate!'

sanskrit: kānaneṣu ca ramyeṣu parvateṣu nadīṣu ca nivasann ānayām āsa vṛṣṇidārān dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Halting amid lovely forests, mountains, and rivers, Dhanaṃjaya led the women of the Vṛṣṇis along the way.

sanskrit: sa pañcanadam āsādya dhīmān atisamṛddhimat deśe gopaśudhānyāḍhye nivāsam akarot prabhuḥ
english: Reaching the Land of the Five Rivers, prosperous and abounding in cattle, livestock, and grain, the wise lord made his encampment there.

sanskrit: tato lobhaḥ samabhavad dasyūnāṃ nihateśvarāḥ dṛṣṭvā striyo nīyamānāḥ pārthenaikena bhārata
english: Then greed arose in the robbers, O Bhārata, when they saw the women, their protectors slain, being led on by Pārtha alone.

sanskrit: tatas te pāpakarmāṇo lobhopahatacetasaḥ ābhīrā mantrayām āsuḥ sametyāśubhadarśanāḥ
english: Then those Ābhīras of evil deeds, their minds corrupted by greed and ill-favoured to look upon, gathered together and took counsel.

sanskrit: ayam eko 'rjuno yoddhā vṛddhabālaṃ hateśvaram nayaty asmān atikramya yodhāś ceme hataujasaḥ
english: 'This Arjuna, a single warrior, leads on past us this throng of old men and children, their lords slain, and these fighters too have lost their vigour.'

sanskrit: tato yaṣṭipraharaṇā dasyavas te sahasraśaḥ abhyadhāvanta vṛṣṇīnāṃ taṃ janaṃ loptrahāriṇaḥ
english: Then those robbers, armed with cudgels, in their thousands rushed upon that people of the Vṛṣṇis, bent on seizing plunder.

sanskrit: mahatā siṃhanādena drāvayantaḥ pṛthagjanam abhipetur dhanārthaṃ te kālaparyāyacoditāḥ
english: With a mighty lion's roar, driving the common folk before them, they fell upon them for the sake of wealth, impelled by the turning of time.

sanskrit: tato nivṛttaḥ kaunteyaḥ sahasā sapadānugaḥ uvāca tān mahābāhur arjunaḥ prahasann iva
english: Then the son of Kuntī turned back at once, his followers behind him, and the mighty-armed Arjuna spoke to them, almost laughing.

sanskrit: nivartadhvam adharmajñā yadi stha na mumūrṣavaḥ nedānīṃ śaranirbhinnāḥ śocadhvaṃ nihatā mayā
english: 'Turn back, you who know not righteousness, if you have no wish to die — lest, pierced through by my arrows and slain by me, you grieve in vain.'

sanskrit: tathoktās tena vīreṇa kadarthīkṛtya tad vacaḥ abhipetur janaṃ mūḍhā vāryamāṇāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Though thus addressed by that hero, the fools made light of his words and, though warned again and again, fell upon the people.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno dhanur divyaṃ gāṇḍīvam ajaraṃ mahat āropayitum ārebhe yatnād iva kathaṃ cana
english: Then Arjuna began, only with effort and scarcely at all, to string that great, undecaying, celestial bow, the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: cakāra sajyaṃ kṛcchreṇa saṃbhrame tumule sati cintayām āsa cāstrāṇi na ca sasmāra tāny api
english: He strung it with difficulty amid the tumultuous confusion, and he called to mind his celestial weapons, yet he could not remember them.

sanskrit: vaikṛtyaṃ tan mahad dṛṣṭvā bhujavīrye tathā yudhi divyānāṃ ca mahāstrāṇāṃ vināśād vrīḍito 'bhavat
english: Seeing that great failing in the strength of his arms in battle, and the loss of his great celestial weapons, he was filled with shame.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇiyodhāś ca te sarve gajāśvarathayāyinaḥ na śekur āvartayituṃ hriyamāṇaṃ ca taṃ janam
english: And all those Vṛṣṇi warriors, riding on elephants, horses, and chariots, were unable to turn back that people who were being carried off.

sanskrit: kalatrasya bahutvāt tu saṃpatatsu tatas tataḥ prayatnam akarot pārtho janasya parirakṣaṇe
english: But because the women were so many, scattering this way and that, Pārtha made every effort to protect the people.

sanskrit: miṣatāṃ sarvayodhānāṃ tatas tāḥ pramadottamāḥ samantato 'vakṛṣyanta kāmāc cānyāḥ pravavrajuḥ
english: While all the warriors looked on, those fairest of women were dragged away on every side, and others went off of their own will.

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvanirmuktaiḥ śaraiḥ pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ jaghāna dasyūn sodvego vṛṣṇibhṛtyaiḥ saha prabhuḥ
english: Then Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya the lord, in great agitation, slew the robbers with arrows shot from the Gāṇḍīva, together with the servants of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena tasya te rājan kṣayaṃ jagmur ajihmagāḥ akṣayā hi purā bhūtvā kṣīṇāḥ kṣatajabhojanāḥ
english: In a moment, O king, his straight-flying arrows were spent: those shafts, once inexhaustible, were exhausted, having fed upon blood.

sanskrit: sa śarakṣayam āsādya duḥkhaśokasamāhataḥ dhanuṣkoṭyā tadā dasyūn avadhīt pākaśāsaniḥ
english: His arrows spent, smitten with pain and grief, the son of the chastiser of Pāka then slew the robbers with the very tip of his bow.

sanskrit: prekṣatas tv eva pārthasya vṛṣṇyandhakavarastriyaḥ jagmur ādāya te mlecchāḥ samantāj janamejaya
english: Yet even as Pārtha looked on, those barbarians carried off the choicest women of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas on every side, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayas tu daivaṃ tan manasācintayat prabhuḥ duḥkhaśokasamāviṣṭo niḥśvāsaparamo 'bhavat
english: The lord Dhanaṃjaya pondered that working of fate in his mind, and, overcome with pain and grief, fell to deep sighing.

sanskrit: astrāṇāṃ ca praṇāśena bāhuvīryasya saṃkṣayāt dhanuṣaś cāvidheyatvāc charāṇāṃ saṃkṣayeṇa ca
english: By the loss of his weapons, the ebbing of the strength of his arms, the unruliness of his bow, and the exhaustion of his arrows —

sanskrit: babhūva vimanāḥ pārtho daivam ity anucintayan nyavartata tato rājan nedam astīti cābravīt
english: — Pārtha grew dejected, reflecting that it was fate; then he desisted, O king, saying, 'This is no longer what it was.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śeṣam ādāya kalatrasya mahāmatiḥ hṛtabhūyiṣṭharatnasya kurukṣetram avātarat
english: Then the great-minded one, taking what remained of the women, the most of whose jewels had been carried off, came down to Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: evaṃ kalatram ānīya vṛṣṇīnāṃ hṛtaśeṣitam nyaveśayata kauravyas tatra tatra dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Having thus brought the women of the Vṛṣṇis, what was left of them after the plunder, the Kaurava Dhanaṃjaya settled them here and there.

sanskrit: hārdikyatanayaṃ pārtho nagaraṃ mārtikāvatam bhojarājakalatraṃ ca hṛtaśeṣaṃ narottamaḥ
english: Pārtha, best of men, settled the son of Hṛdika in the city of Mārtikāvata, together with the remaining women of the Bhoja king.

sanskrit: tato vṛddhāṃś ca bālāṃś ca striyaś cādāya pāṇḍavaḥ vīrair vihīnān sarvāṃs tāñ śakraprasthe nyaveśayat
english: Then the Pāṇḍava, taking the old men, the children, and the women, all bereft of their heroes, settled them at Śakraprastha.

sanskrit: yauyudhāniṃ sarasvatyāṃ putraṃ sātyakinaḥ priyam nyaveśayata dharmātmā vṛddhabālapuraskṛtam
english: The righteous one settled the son of Yuyudhāna, the beloved son of Sātyaki, on the banks of the Sarasvatī, with the old and young at his head.

sanskrit: indraprasthe dadau rājyaṃ vajrāya paravīrahā vajreṇākrūradārās tu vāryamāṇāḥ pravavrajuḥ
english: The slayer of hostile heroes gave the kingdom at Indraprastha to Vajra; but the wives of Akrūra, though restrained by Vajra, departed.

sanskrit: rukmiṇī tv atha gāndhārī śaibyā haimavatīty api devī jāmbavatī caiva viviśur jātavedasam
english: Then Rukmiṇī, and Gāndhārī, and Śaibyā, and Haimavatī, and queen Jāmbavatī entered the fire.

sanskrit: satyabhāmā tathaivānyā devyaḥ kṛṣṇasya saṃmatāḥ vanaṃ praviviśū rājaṃs tāpasye kṛtaniścayāḥ
english: And Satyabhāmā and the other queens cherished by Kṛṣṇa entered the forest, O king, resolved upon the life of asceticism.

sanskrit: dvārakāvāsino ye tu puruṣāḥ pārtham anvayuḥ yathārhaṃ saṃvibhajyainān vajre paryadadaj jayaḥ
english: As for those men of Dvārakā who had followed Pārtha, the victorious one divided them as was fitting and entrusted them to Vajra.

sanskrit: sa tat kṛtvā prāptakālaṃ bāṣpeṇāpihito 'rjunaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ rājan dadarśāsīnam āśrame
english: Having done what the hour required, Arjuna, his eyes veiled with tears, beheld Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, O king, seated in his hermitage.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca praviśann arjuno rājann āśramaṃ satyavādinaḥ dadarśāsīnam ekānte muniṃ satyavatīsutam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As he entered the hermitage of the truthful sage, O king, Arjuna beheld the son of Satyavatī seated apart in solitude.

sanskrit: sa tam āsādya dharmajñam upatasthe mahāvratam arjuno 'smīti nāmāsmai nivedyābhyavadat tataḥ
english: Approaching that knower of righteousness of great vows, he stood before him, and announcing his name, 'I am Arjuna,' he then addressed him.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te 'stv iti prāha muniḥ satyavatīsutaḥ āsyatām iti covāca prasannātmā mahāmuniḥ
english: 'Welcome to you,' said the sage, the son of Satyavatī, and the great sage, serene of soul, added, 'Be seated.'

sanskrit: tam apratītamanasaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ nirviṇṇamanasaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthaṃ vyāso 'bravīd idam
english: Seeing Pārtha downcast in mind, sighing again and again, and despondent of heart, Vyāsa spoke these words.

sanskrit: avīrajo 'bhighātas te brāhmaṇo vā hatas tvayā yuddhe parājito vāsi gataśrīr iva lakṣyase
english: 'Has some stain that comes not from valour befallen you? Or has a Brāhmaṇa been slain by you? Or have you been vanquished in battle? You seem like one whose splendour has departed.'
